claim: Evaluative adjuncts “do not, therefore, occur in interrogatives, imperatives, or pragmatically presupposed subordinate clauses”, with [5iii] ∗Since Deidre fortunately recovered from her illness, she has lived in California, where since is temporal.
evidence_summary: §19, p. 778 explains a restriction on connective adjuncts in the same terms but marks it #: “The felicitous use of these connectives requires that the similarity be between propositions that are informationally in the foreground, not presupposed”, with [12ii] #Kim has stopped smoking and Pat used to smoke too. On p. 702 a #-marked example “certainly does not violate any rule of grammar”.
finding: Low confidence. Both restrictions rest on the difference between asserted and presupposed information, and p. 772 explains its restriction in pragmatic terms, so by CGEL’s own conventions [5iii] fits # better than ∗. The defence that CGEL treats the evaluative restriction as grammaticalised, since it is stated alongside interrogative and imperative clause types, partly works.
inference: Is the restriction on evaluative adjuncts in presupposed clauses grammatical or pragmatic?

evidence.passage: §17, p. 772. “∗Since Deidre fortunately recovered from her illness, she has lived in California.”
evidence.example: Page 778 [12ii] #Kim has stopped smoking and Pat used to smoke too.
evidence.establishes: The chapter gives one information-status explanation two different marks.
